bull.argument: Nike's fiscal 2026 filing shows a company absorbing a difficult cycle while preserving profitability. Revenue held flat at $46.4 billion, and gross margin rose 20 basis points to 42.9%. Management's EBIT margin of 8.3% and ROIC of 18.7% remain well above the level one would expect from a business in distress. The IEEPA tariff recovery of $986 million, largely offsetting tariff costs, is a concrete earnings tailwind, and substantially all of the remaining receivable was collected after year-end. Management has also set out a defined plan (product rebalancing, marketplace repositioning, increased demand creation) with an end date of December 2026, and North America, the largest segment, is already showing higher revenues. Wholesale revenues grew 6% to $27.5 billion, indicating reinvestment in distribution is working. The bear case will point to Greater China, Converse and NIKE Direct declines, and those are real. But they are identified, quantified and expected to be resolved in a defined window, and the core business continues to generate substantial earnings.

claims.claim: Gross margin improved despite a difficult revenue environment.
claims.quote: Gross margin increased 20 basis points to 42.9% for fiscal 2026 compared to 42.7% for fiscal 2025

claims.claim: Management reports a large tariff recovery that offsets tariff costs.
claims.quote: we recognized a benefit of $986 million in Cost of sales within the Consolidated Statements of Income for the recovery of IEEPA tariffs paid

claims.claim: Wholesale growth shows the reinvestment in distribution is gaining traction.
claims.quote: NIKE Brand wholesale revenues were $27.5 billion in fiscal 2026 compared to $25.9 billion in fiscal 2025, up 6% on a reported basis

bear.argument: The bull case leans on a $986 million IEEPA tariff recovery, but that is a one-time benefit, not operating strength. Net income fell 3% to $3,108 million, and diluted EPS dropped from $2.16 to $2.10. Underneath the flat top line, the core is eroding: NIKE Direct revenues fell 6% to $17.7 billion, NIKE Brand Digital sales dropped 12% on reduced traffic, and comparable store sales decreased 4%. Management itself says Greater China and Converse will keep hurting results through fiscal 2027, which pushes the 'defined window' well beyond the December 2026 end date cited as a reassurance. Management also booked $385 million in severance and warns of 'additional charges in future quarters.' The filing further says footwear unit sales fell 1% and that inventory clearance requires 'increased markdowns' and higher returns and discounts. Management's own risk factors warn that markdowns can 'significantly impair our brand image.' Taken together, the margin support looks partly borrowed from a one-time recovery, while the demand problems remain unresolved.

claims.claim: Net income declined year over year, so earnings are not growing despite the flat revenue headline.
Management expects negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to persist beyond the stated end date, extending the recovery timeline into fiscal 2027.
claims.quote: We expect negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to continue throughout fiscal 2027.

claims.claim: NIKE Direct and digital demand is weakening, with digital sales down 12% on reduced traffic and markdowns used to clear inventory.
claims.quote: NIKE Brand Digital sales were $8.6 billion in fiscal 2026 compared to $9.6 billion in fiscal 2025, with declines primarily due to reduced traffic.

bull.argument: The bear is right that the $986 million IEEPA recovery is one-time, and I would not call it operating strength. But the case for Nike rests on more than that benefit. Excluding the recovery, the filing still shows gross margin of 42.9% with lower warehousing and logistics costs and favorable currency effects, so margin improvement is not solely a tariff refund. On demand, the bear's NIKE Direct decline is real, but it reflects a deliberate choice: management says it is repositioning NIKE Brand Digital as a full-price platform and clearing inventory through markdowns. That trade-off is painful in the near term, yet it is the mechanism the company describes for restoring brand health. Wholesale revenue rose 6% to $27.5 billion, and North America, the largest segment, grew, so the business is not uniformly weakening. Net income of $3.1 billion and EBIT margin of 8.3% remain substantial. The bear is correct that Greater China and Converse drag through fiscal 2027, and that severance and future charges are possible. I accept those as real risks. The investment case is that the core franchise is intact, the drag is identified and concentrated, and the company is actively working on it.

claims.claim: Gross margin gains came from several sources, not only the tariff recovery.
claims.quote: Lower warehousing and logistics costs (increasing gross margin approximately 20 basis points), primarily due to channel mix

claims.claim: Management frames NIKE Direct declines as a deliberate repositioning rather than an unplanned collapse.
claims.quote: Repositioning NIKE Brand Digital as a full-price platform and reinvesting in wholesale distribution.

claims.claim: North America, the largest segment, is growing and has made the most progress on the restructuring actions.
claims.quote: North America has made the most progress against these actions, while Greater China and Converse will take more time.

bear.argument: The bull's margin defense is weaker than it looks. The $986 million IEEPA recovery sits in cost of sales and is part of the reported 42.9% gross margin. The filing says it largely offset tariffs recognized in the same year, so the net effect is smaller than the headline. The bridge also leans on currency: favorable FX, hedges and lower 'other costs' each added about 20 basis points, and currency can reverse. Pre-tax income was essentially flat at $3,900 million versus $3,885 million. Net income fell 3% because the effective tax rate rose from 17.1% to 20.3%, which is not an operating improvement. Demand is also softer than the wholesale headline suggests. NIKE Direct fell 8% currency-neutral, and footwear unit sales declined 1%. Management's plan requires markdowns and discounts to clear inventory, and its own risk factors warn that discounted sales 'could significantly impair our brand image.' Greater China and Converse drag continues through fiscal 2027, beyond the December 2026 window. The core franchise may be intact, but the earnings and demand evidence in this filing is not yet a recovery.

claims.claim: Pre-tax income was flat, and net income fell mainly because the effective tax rate rose, so the decline is not an operating gain.
Currency-neutral revenues fell, with declines in Greater China, Converse and EMEA, so underlying demand is weaker than the flat reported headline.
claims.quote: On a currency-neutral basis, NIKE, Inc. Revenues decreased 2%, primarily due to lower revenues in Greater China, Converse and Europe, Middle East & Africa

claims.claim: Footwear unit demand is declining, and pricing support is shrinking.
claims.quote: Unit sales of footwear decreased 1%, while lower average selling price

judge.reasoning: All quotes are verified on both sides, but the bear's evidence is more targeted: it shows pre-tax income was flat and the net income decline came from a higher tax rate, and it cites currency-neutral revenue declines and unit sales weakness. The bull partially conceded the one-time nature of the IEEPA recovery and its bridge claim relies on a 20 bp warehousing item, which the bear effectively reframed as a non-operating or currency-dependent contribution. The bear's rebuttal on the margin bridge was more responsive to the bull's central argument, so the bear edges the debate.
